subject: MedSpark MAP: performance validation & close timeline (TTFT / streaming / concurrency)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Price <olivia.price@medspark.com>, Ben Rivera <ben.rivera@medspark.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T09:15:00Z
Subject: MedSpark MAP: performance validation & close timeline (TTFT / streaming / concurrency)

Hi Olivia / Ben —

Following our call yesterday, looping in Monica (solutions) and Marcus (bench lead) to propose a concise MAP for the performance gate that will unblock procurement and final signature. Goal: validate streaming TTFT and steady-state throughput under your expected concurrency envelope and land on SLAs we can commit to in the contract.

High-level ask for this MAP:
- Run a 3-day validation: 1) baseline TTFT profile (p50/p95/p99) for interactive chat flows, 2) concurrency sweep (1, 8, 32, 64 concurrent users) for sustained 30m windows, 3) a short burst test to validate autoscale-to-burst behavior.
- Acceptance criteria (proposed): p95 TTFT <= 450ms on streaming endpoints for 2-token ack / initial chunk; sustained QPS at 64 concurrency with median throughput X tokens/s per GPU (see runbook).
- Deliverables: raw CSV of per-request timings, summarized p50/p95/p99 charts, and a short one-page MAP appendix to attach to the SOW.

Attached is a draft runbook (redwood-maps-performance-runbook.pdf) and a sample CSV schema. Proposed timeline:
- Kickoff test plan: Tue 2027-05-18
- Run tests: Wed-Fri 2027-05-19 to 2027-05-21 (we can compress to two days if needed)
- Results & MAP appendix: Mon 2027-05-24
- Target signature: Fri 2027-05-28

Please confirm the concurrency mix you want (we used 70% chat, 30% background retriever calls as a default) and whether you want encryption-in-flight test nodes in your VPC (for Private deployment validation).

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-maps-performance-runbook.pdf (15 pages; test matrices + request templates)
From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@medspark.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Rivera <ben.rivera@medspark.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: MedSpark MAP: performance validation & close timeline (TTFT / streaming / concurrency)

Thanks Vivek — this looks good and aligns with what procurement asked for. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Concurrency mix: can we do a clinical pilot mix — 60% clinician chat sessions (longer contexts, avg 1.2k tokens), 30% patient triage (shorter), 10% embeddings/rerank calls? That will stress attention-window performance.
2) Encryption: yes, we'd like the Private deployment validation in our AWS account. We'll share temporary cross-account IAM roles.
3) Burst behavior: important — please include a 10x burst for 2 minutes to see tail latency effects.

If you can confirm those specifics and whether you need a signed NDA amendment for cross-account test infra, we can lock kickoff Tue.

— Olivia
Olivia Price
Head of Product, MedSpark Health

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Price <olivia.price@medspark.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: MedSpark MAP: performance validation & close timeline (TTFT / streaming / concurrency)

Hi Olivia —

We can run the clinical pilot mix you outlined. A couple of operational notes from the runbook:
- Test harness: we will use Redwood's traffic generator with request interleaving to simulate streaming (we send initial prompt, then stream 2-4 tokens per chunk depending on model); the harness will capture first-byte time (TTFT) and chunk latencies so you can see initial-response vs sustained stream.
- Concurrency windows: we'll do steady-state 30m windows at 1, 8, 32, 64. For the 10x burst test we'll ramp from 8 to 80 over 30s, hold for 120s, then ramp down — collects p99 tail behavior.
- Data handling: no PHI will be retained in Redwood logs; we will use synthetic clinical prompts modeled after your corpus.

Please upload the IAM role and a short allowlist for external IPs; Marcus will coordinate the actual run and post the raw CSV to the shared Drive.

Operational owner: Marcus Lin (marcus@redwood.ai)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Price <olivia.price@medspark.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MedSpark MAP: performance validation & close timeline (TTFT / streaming / concurrency)

Quick status — ran the first pass of the clinical pilot tests in your staging VPC today (attached summarized CSV). Key findings:

- Baseline streaming TTFT (initial chunk) on r-infer-1 (A100-equivalent): p50=120ms, p95=380ms, p99=610ms (median chunk size: 2 tokens).
- 32-concurrency steady-state sustained throughput: median tokens/s per instance = 48. Sustained p95 latency per chunk increased ~1.6x vs single-user baseline.
- 64-concurrency: p95 TTFT ~540ms, p99 ~980ms — we saw CPU queueing on the aux router at peak; adding one additional inference instance reduced p99 to ~700ms.
- 10x burst (8->80) produced transient p99 spikes >2s for a handful of requests; tail correlated with cold-worker spin-up and a 200ms network retry from the sec-proxy.

Attached files: medspark-ttft-raw-results.csv (per-request timings), short-run-summary.md (2 pages). Proposed MAP acceptance tweak: require p95 TTFT <= 500ms at 64 concurrency with an autoscale buffer of +1 instance for peak. If MedSpark signs off, we will attach the MAP appendix to the SOW and run a final validation window prior to go-live.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Performance Engineering Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments: medspark-ttft-raw-results.csv (CSV, ~120k rows)
From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@medspark.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Rivera <ben.rivera@medspark.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T16:32:00Z
Subject: Re: MedSpark MAP: performance validation & close timeline (TTFT / streaming / concurrency)

Thanks Marcus and team — this is helpful and in line with our expectations. We accept the proposed MAP acceptance tweak (p95 <= 500ms at 64 concurrency with +1 instance buffer). A couple of next steps from MedSpark:

- I'll route the MAP appendix and the performance summary to procurement for inclusion in the SOW (please send a one-page appendix we can attach).
- We'll approve the final validation window after procurement confirms the SLA language; target final validation: 2027-05-25.
- Please include one short paragraph in the appendix on mitigation for burst tail events (we want the strategy documented).

Once procurement confirms, let's aim to have DocuSign-ready SOW by 2027-05-28.

— Olivia
Olivia Price
Head of Product, MedSpark Health
